radiology_report:
LUMC (Leiden)
Imaging Department
Date: 15 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: PSA 7.0 ng/mL, rising trend, prior biopsy Gleason 3+4. Request for PI-RADS assessment.

FINDINGS:
The prostate volume is 16.4 mL. The transition zone is unremarkable. In the left peripheral zone, at the mid-gland level, there is a focal lesion measuring approximately 12 mm in craniocaudal dimension. On T2-weighted imaging, the lesion appears as a well-defined area of low signal intensity. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates marked restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 images and corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early, intense enhancement of the lesion. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visualized.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1 category 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 16.4 mL, PSA density 0.427 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8631027.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (24 May 2024): Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, left.

Biopsy 2 (Current): Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, left.

Summary: The histological findings across both biopsy timepoints remain stable at ISUP grade group 2.
